text:
sara-support: Hi team, acme reported Redwood Private control-plane is intermittently failing to complete TLS handshakes to their KMS endpoint. They say agent registration times out, and the control-plane logs show cert validation errors. Ticket says this started after they rolled out an OPA constraint yesterday.

sara-support: Customer repro steps: 1) Deploy private control-plane (v1.8) 2) Apply their OPA constraint (defaults/deny-egress-infra) 3) Start redwood-agent helm chart -> agent fails to register.

sara-support: Error from agent logs: 
```
2025-11-02T18:10:21Z WARN controlplane: tls handshake failed: remote error: tls: handshake failure (alert 40)
2025-11-02T18:10:21Z INFO retrying registration (attempt 3)
```

sara-support: They ran `kubectl exec -n redwood-system redwood-agent-0 -- curl -v https://kms.acme.internal:443 --connect-timeout 5` and got: `* TCP_NODELAY set` then repeated `* connect to 10.4.2.17 port 443 failed: Connection timed out`

mike-eng-infra: thanks. Do they have a default-deny egress NP in the cluster? OPA could be denying egress or injecting a CRD that adds a networkpolicy. Can you paste `kubectl get networkpolicy --all-namespaces` and the netpol in redwood-system? Also need pod spec for agent (hostNetwork? initContainers?).

sara-support: Pasted key outputs below. `kubectl get networkpolicy -A` shows a policy in infra-ns: `default-deny-egress-infra` and another in redwood-system: none. They said OPA applies policies by label selector `app.kubernetes.io/part-of: infra`. OPA constraint YAML: `match: kinds: - apiGroups: ["networking.k8s.io"] namespaces: ["infra-ns"]` (they shared).

sara-support: `kubectl describe pod redwood-agent-0 -n redwood-system` events show `Back-off restarting failed container` but also `EgressDenied by network policy` annotation appears on the pod (their CNI adds this).

jonah-priv-deploy: two quick checks: 1) does the CNI implement egress allowlists at the node level (e.g., calico GlobalNetworkPolicy / Cilium ClusterwideNetworkPolicy) or is it purely NetworkPolicy? 2) Are control-plane endpoints referenced by DNS or by cluster-external IPs? If DNS resolves to private IPs in a CIDR that their policy blocks, that would explain it.

lee-sre: also ask them to run a packet capture from the agent pod: `kubectl exec -n redwood-system redwood-agent-0 -- tcpdump -n -s0 -w - 'port 443' | hexdump -C | head -n50` to confirm SYNs leaving and no SYN-ACK. If SYN leaves and no reply, it's likely egress blocked at networkpolicy/host firewall. If SYN-ACK arrives but TLS fails, that's cert issue.

sara-support: Customer sent tcpdump snippet: `10:12:01.123456 IP 10.244.3.12.54321 > 10.4.2.17.443: Flags [S], seq 12345, win 64240, options [mss 1460,sackOK,TS val 123 ecr 0,nop,wscale 7]` repeated 3 times, no SYN-ACK.

sara-support: They also included `kubectl get clusternetworkpolicies` (calico) and found a Calico GlobalNetworkPolicy `infra-egress-allowlist` that only permits egress to `10.0.0.0/8` and `10.10.20.0/24` but their KMS IP `10.4.2.17` is not in the list.

mike-eng-infra: ok that is the smoking gun. OPA likely enforced the infra policy then calico GNP tightened egress. Two remediation options: A) ask customer to add `10.4.2.0/24` to infra-egress-allowlist, or B) create a Calico GlobalNetworkPolicy `allow-redwood-controlplane` with selector `app == "redwood-agent"` allowing egress to KMS and control-plane ranges on tcp/443.

jonah-priv-deploy: for short-term workaround, they can annotate the redwood-agent daemonset pods with label `networking.k8s.io/egress-exempt: "true"` if their infra automation respects that, or patch OPA Constraint to exclude `Namespace == "redwood-system"`. But safest is explicit allow for control-plane endpoints.

lee-sre: also note cert validation error in logs earlier — that can happen if TLS handshake never completes and the agent reports remote error. Once egress is fixed the TLS should succeed. Recommend customer check their proxy (if they have HTTP proxy env vars) — proxies can cause MITM cert chains if intercepted.

sara-support: I posted suggested commands to them: 
```
# quick allow via calico (customer-run)
kubectl apply -f - <<EOF
apiVersion: projectcalico.org/v3
kind: GlobalNetworkPolicy
metadata:
  name: allow-redwood-controlplane
spec:
  selector: app == 'redwood-agent'
  order: 100
  egress:
  - action: Allow
    protocol: TCP
    destination:
      nets:
      - 10.4.2.0/24 # KMS
      - 10.5.0.0/24 # control-plane
    ports:
    - 443
  types:
  - Egress
EOF
```

jonah-priv-deploy: +1. Also show them how to test after applying: `kubectl exec -n redwood-system redwood-agent-0 -- curl -v https://kms.acme.internal:443 --connect-timeout 5` and `kubectl logs -n redwood-system -l app=redwood-agent --tail 200` to confirm registration success.

deploy-bot: deploy:redwood-agent v1.2.3 started rollout to redwood-system at 2025-11-02T19:02:10Z

sara-support: Customer applied the calico policy change and reports `curl` now returns HTTP 400 from KMS (expected because they hit TLS endpoint) and agent registration completed: `INFO controlplane: registered with control-plane; id=agent-03`. They said adding the infra CIDR would've been a bandaid; they'd rather patch OPA constraint to exclude redwood-system.

mike-eng-infra: please advise customer to add an exception in their OPA constraint logic: exclude namespaces `redwood-system, kube-system`. Provide example patch: 
```
match:
  kinds:
  - apiGroups: ["networking.k8s.io"]
  namespaces: ["infra-ns"]
  excludedNamespaces: ["redwood-system"]
```
(implementation depends on their constraint template).

lee-sre: closing checklist: 1) Validate calico/global allowlist includes control-plane/KMS CIDRs 2) Prefer explicit per-app allow GNP for redwood-agent 3) Exclude redwood-system from infra OPA constraints 4) Check for HTTP proxies that could intercept TLS.

sara-support: Thanks all — customer confirmed stable after change and will update OPA rules. Marking as resolved but leaving notes for docs: add KB on common NetPol/Calico/OPA interactions with Redwood Private. :thumbsup:
